project_name: Construction Partners Dothan headquarters and data processing center
status_detail: Construction Partners announced a $20 million corporate headquarters and centralized data processing center in Dothan; public reports describe it as serving the company's operating companies across eight states, not a hyperscale/colocation campus.
notes: Included because sources call it a data processing center/data center component, though likely a small enterprise facility bundled with headquarters rather than a public cloud hyperscale facility.

status_detail: Google operates its Jackson County data center at/near the retired TVA Widows Creek power plant site; Google says it broke ground in 2018 and opened the first data center in 2018. Alabama Daily News reported in June 2026 that Google announced a $1.5 billion expansion to build out the facility over 2026-2027.
notes: Official Google page reports $2B+ invested in Alabama since building the Jackson County data center in 2018. News source reports 2026 $1.5B expansion and 300 MW energy contracted to the region; tracker separately lists operating Buildings 1-2 at 60 MW each and planned Buildings 3-4 at 150 MW each, but capacity is left null here to avoid mixing project phases.

status_detail: QTS confirms it is developing a Bessemer data center facility. Bessemer's official site posts updated development plans for Project Marvel. Local reporting and SELC cite Bessemer City Council rezoning approvals; SELC summarizes original plans as 18 server farms, 4.5 million square feet, and 1,200 MW of electricity need.
notes: Developer previously obscured behind Logistic Land Investments/Project Marvel; QTS page now confirms Bessemer facility. Status set approved because rezoning was approved, while QTS still describes planning as progressing.

status_detail: Nebius project page says it acquired 75 acres at 201 Milan Parkway in Birmingham's Oxmoor neighborhood in September 2025 and targeted Q1 2026 permits. Local reporting says construction has begun/land has been cleared, a judge allowed construction to continue, and the project is a 300 MW data center at Oxmoor Corporate Park.
notes: Capacity comes from local/news reporting, not the visible Nebius overview text. Official Nebius materials frame the site as an AI factory under evaluation/development.

status_detail: DC BLOX operates a 31,000 square foot Birmingham colocation facility near UAB/Innovation Depot and says the campus opened in 2019. Company community page says the facility currently uses less than 1 MW of power; ABC 33/40 reported a planned adjacent 30,000 square foot expansion needing 7.5 MW.
notes: Existing facility is operational; the expansion is noted in status_detail but not split into a separate row because it appears adjacent to/part of the same campus.
